title: SPA/107/2017 of Vipin Ram Daftari Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 107 of 2017
Vipin Ram Daftari Ö...Appellant.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ÖÖ Respondents.
With
Special Appeal No. 108 of 2017
Dinesh Chandra Pandey Ö...Appellant.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ÖÖ Respondents.
With
Special Appeal No. 109 of 2017
Surendra Singh Jalal Ö...Appellant.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ÖÖ Respondents.
Present:
Mr. M.S. Ray, Advocate for the appellants.
Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand/respondents.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Honíble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Honíble Alok Singh, J.
Dated: 14th June, 2017
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)

Since common issue is raised in these appeals,
therefore, these appeals are taken together and are being
decided by the common judgment.
2. Appellants were working as Peons in Government
Education Institution. By the impugned order, the
appellants stood transferred. The learned Single Judge felt

that there is no merit in the case and dismissed the writ
petitions.
3. We heard Mr. M.K. Ray, learned counsel for the
appellants and Mr. Rajeev Singh Bisht, learned Brief Holder
for the State of Uttarakhand / respondents.
4. In the impugned order, it is stated that Section 28 (1) of
the Uttarakhand School Education Act, 2006 (hereinafter
referred to as ìActî) has been violated by the appellants as
during the sudden inspection, it was found that the
appellants were not performing the duties in accordance
with Section 28 (1) of the Act.
5. The crux of the matter is that the appellants who were
Peons were asked to do night duty to safeguard the
examination papers. There is not much dispute that they
refused to do it. It is, in these circumstances, the appellants
were transferred.
6. Mr. M.K. Ray, the learned counsel for the appellants
would submit that the appellants, being Peons, cannot be
called upon to discharge duty at night without their consent.
In this regard, he placed reliance on the un-reported
judgment of the learned Single Judge wherein the learned
Single Judge has held as follows:
ìOnce it is an admitted case that the petitioner is
appointed as a Peon, the work of a ìchaukidarî cannot
be taken from the petitioner against his own wish.
This would not only be an unfair practice but would be
violative of settled norms. It is expected from a

welfare State that they should work in accordance with
law and not in violation of law. It was found that the
respondents cannot take the work of Chaukidar from
petitioner as it is violative of the working condition.î
7. But as far as this case is concerned, there is a difference.
The impugned action is premised under Section 28 (1) of the
Act. Section 28 (1) of the Act reads as follows:
ì28. Provisions for assistance during
examination. ñ (1) For the conduct of Boardís
Examination, evaluation of answer books in such
Examination and preparation of result thereof, the
Committee of Management, Head of Institution, every
teacher and other employee in relation to an
institution, shall render such assistance, perform such
duties and discharge such functions as may be
required, entrusted or assigned to it or him by or under
this Act.î
8. In the counter affidavit, it is stated that the appellants
refused to do night duty which is required for safety of
question papers and answer books of Board Examination,
2017, due to which, the Board Examination was adversely
affected. While perusal of Section 28 of the Act, we notice
that it contemplates that for the conduct of Board
Examination, evaluation of answer books and preparation of
result, the Committee of Management, Head of the
Institution, every teacher and every employee in relation to
an institution shall render such assistance, perform such
duties and discharge such functions as may be required,
entrusted or assigned to him either under the Act or by the
Act. The specific case of the respondents is that the

appellants refused to do night duty for the purpose of safety
of the question papers and answer books. The situation, at
hand, may not be the position which is reflected in the
judgment of the learned Single Judge which we have
adverted to. We also agree with the learned Single Judge
that generally night duty cannot be imposed upon the Peon
against his wishes. But, this is a scenario which is
specifically governed by the statutory provisions. Under
Section 28 of the Act, the time during the duties required to
be performed, is not specifically mentioned. Obviously,
examination duty and all aspects flowing from the
examination duty are of unique nature and it requires
cooperation from all employees. The further contention of
the learned counsel for the appellants is that there is no
inquiry held as such. He relies on the judgment reported in
2008 (2) U.D. 517, wherein the Full Bench of this Court in the
context of transfer order held that transfer on administrative
grounds can be effected only on the following situations :
i. In case of serious complaints.
ii. Misbehavior with superior officers and;
iii. Absence of interest in work.
9. What the Court has held that the authority competent
must prima facie arrive at and duly record satisfaction about
the existence and truthfulness of the allegations after due
verification and confirmation against the person. If the
prima facie satisfaction upon due verification and
confirmation is not arrived at, the order of transfer on
administrative ground is vitiated. Therefore, this principle
has been initiated to ensure that though allegations fall in
any of the three categories mentioned, without being prima

facie substantiated or verified, action should not be taken
against the government servant.
10. In this case, we notice that the stand of the appellants
also appears to be, even to this day, that they are not ready
to perform night duty. This also lends assurance to the
statement contained in the order that there was an inspection
and it was found that they were not carrying on the duty. It
is not that the appellants are as such contending that they
were ready to perform the duty.
11. Therefore, in these circumstances, reliance placed on
the judgment also does not appear to be correct. In such
circumstances, we would think that the appeals must fail
and are dismissed.
12. Thereupon, the learned counsel for the appellants
submits that representation may be directed to be considered
by the Chief Education Officer. He would also submit that
the appellants will join within a period of one week from
today. If appellants join within a period of one week from
today, the representation will be considered within a period
of three weeks thereafter.
 (Alok Singh, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C. J.)
 14.06.2017 14.06.2017
Shiv
